Mattner1992 and HuShiu2022 concern completeness/zero testing, not the observable PLM contour ratio eliminating the outcome-contamination transform.

JinMackeySyrgkanis2025 gives the Gaussian barrier and finite-order non-Gaussian ACE bound, but not the common-code spectral-versus-Gaussian MSE dichotomy.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 4 and 8, Theorems 3.2 and 5.4, equations (6), (21), and (22)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 3.2 gives the bounded-outcome Gaussian generalized-quantile lower bound under bounded supplied nuisances; Theorem 5.4 gives the independent sub-Gaussian ACE quantile upper bound with the displayed epsilon1^r epsilon2 and Ctheta epsilon1^(r+1) terms, subject to condition (21).
The paper characterizes conditional Gaussian treatment residuals through moment identities and constructs finite-variance second-order orthogonal PLM moments under a non-Gaussian residual condition.

The published work studies locally robust semiparametric inference when independent structural shocks are close to Gaussian in linear simultaneous-equation models; no unavailable theorem text was used to claim overlap with the PLM contour proposal.

The paper develops a quantitative Marcinkiewicz theorem from characteristic-function nonvanishing on a bounded disk, supporting its role as analytic background for the converse zero-localization route.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: State and prove explicitly that the spectral class is a strict subclass of the published L^r ACE class when s>r, then phrase the ACE improvement as a strict result on that published-class subclass rather than relying on the intersection shorthand.
Make the finite contour bank operational by giving an explicit grid-resolution or modulus-of-continuity bound in terms of the displayed class constants, rather than only an existence subcover.

Add a finite-sample oracle inequality separating contour-estimation error, selector failure probability, and dependence on delta, R0, and a_star; this would make the fixed-separation result directly informative for the local-to-Gaussian frontier.

recommended_next_step: Advance the fixed-separation contour-minimax kernel to Stage 0, retaining the local-to-Gaussian problem as its separately scoped open extension.
